payload.title: Evaluate Laya and compact multilingual pair classifiers for existing-task matching
payload.description: User asks whether Laya or a specialized micro dense model can detect existing open/completed tasks despite paraphrasing. Proposed experiment related to scalable retrieval task task_76b337bcfa7db953636318fb7dd755799ae72c04cfc7c53fc29c5cbf60b5b4df: retrieve candidate tasks using lexical/vector/metadata search, then compare a request/task pair using Laya multilingual and a compact pretrained multilingual encoder with a trained classification head. Laya is a candidate decision model, not yet validated on DIP; primary model card warns about zero-shot/domain calibration and overconfidence, and multilingual checkpoint has 322M parameters. Prefer baseline evaluation and fine-tuning/distillation of pretrained encoders over training language capabilities from scratch. Models propose same/partial/related/different links; open/completed status and verification remain authoritative structured state/current code evidence. No model installed, trained or called in this exploratory turn.
acceptance: Build independently reviewed positive, partial-overlap, related-only and hard-negative request/task pairs, including Hebrew-English paraphrases, negation, changed scope/version and different components; split held-out evaluation by project and time to avoid paraphrase leakage.

Compare lexical/embedding candidate retrieval, compact cross-encoder pair classification and Laya on the same inputs. Measure candidate recall, false duplicate links, missed duplicates, partial completion coverage, confidence calibration/abstention, CPU latency, RAM and installation overhead.
Fine-tune or distill only after labeled evaluation shows where existing candidates fail; do not assert that a particular micro-model size or training-set size guarantees quality.

Keep routine Git capture model-free; semantic inference runs at meaningful user-intent or completion milestones. Require agent review of uncertain links, and configured real-code checks for verified completion.
